description_full: Spectrum Brands Holdings, Inc. operates as a branded consumer products and home essentials company in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Latin America, and the Asia-Pacific regions. The company offers rawhide and rawhide free chews and treats, dog and cat clean-up, training, health and grooming, and small animal food and care products; wet and dry pet food; consumer and commercial aquarium kits, stand-alone tanks, filtration systems, and heaters and pumps; and aquatics consumables, including fish food, water management, and care. It also provides spider and scorpion killers, ant and roach killers, flying insect killers, insect foggers, wasp and hornet killers, and bedbug, and flea and tick control products; weed control solutions and insect and animal repellents comprising aerosols, granules, and ready-to-use spray or hose-and-ready-to-sprays; aerosols, lotions, pump sprays, and wipes; yard sprays and citronella candles; and household surface cleaning, maintenance, and restoration products, including bottled liquids, and mops. In addition, the company small kitchen appliances, such as toaster ovens, coffeemakers, slow cookers, air fryers, blenders, hand mixers, grills, food processors, juicers, toasters, irons, kettles, and bread makers, cookware, and cookbooks; and hair dryers, flat irons and straighteners, rotary and foil electric shavers, personal groomers, mustache and beard trimmers, body groomers, nose and ear trimmers, women's shavers, and haircut kits. It sells its products under the Good'n'Fun, Good Boy, DreamBone, Nature's Miracle, SmartBones, FURminator, Wild HarvestTM, 8IN1, Dingo, Better Belly, Meowee!, Eukanuba, IAMS, Tetra, Marineland, GloFish, Instant Ocean, OmegaSea, Hot Shot, Black Flag, Spectracide, Liquid Fence, Garden Safe, Cutter, and Remington brands through brick-and-mortar retail channels, e-commerce channels, wholesalers, and distributors. Spectrum Brands Holdings, Inc. was founded in 1906 and is based in Middleton, Wisconsin.

financial_summary: Spectrum Brands Holdings, Inc. is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $1.9B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years and -6% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 35%.

The business throws off $243M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 5.87× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.6×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.1% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
